units.title: Domain A: Physical Quantities and Measurement

outcomes.text: Tell science, technology and engineering apart using everyday examples.
Describe physics as the study of matter, energy and how they are linked.
Explain how physics helps solve real problems such as energy, environment and technology.
Name the main branches of physics and some interdisciplinary fields such as biophysics.
Distinguish physical quantities from non-physical ones.
Separate base and derived quantities, giving their symbols and SI units.
Write numbers in scientific notation for measurements and calculations.
Express data using SI prefixes.
State what significant figures are and the rules for finding and using them in answers.
Identify sources of systematic and random error and how to reduce them.
Tell scalar quantities from vector quantities.
Write vectors in symbols and draw them as arrows with direction.
Add vectors head-to-tail and find the resultant's size and direction.
Split a 2-D vector into two perpendicular components.
Find the resultant of two perpendicular vectors by calculation and drawing.
Explain null, negative and equal vectors.
Explain with examples how an object can be at rest for one observer and moving for another.
Distinguish translatory, rotatory and vibratory motion.
Tell distance from displacement.
Tell speed from velocity.
Tell average from instantaneous speed or velocity.
Tell uniform from non-uniform velocity.
Calculate average speed and velocity from distance, displacement and time.
Explain acceleration, including deceleration.
Tell uniform, non-uniform and instantaneous acceleration apart.
Draw and read distance-time graphs, including rest, constant speed, speeding up and slowing down.
Draw and read speed-time graphs for rest, constant speed and changing acceleration.
Explain that the gradient of a speed-time graph gives acceleration.
Find distance travelled from the area under a speed-time graph.
Derive the equations of motion for uniform acceleration.
Solve straight-line problems using the equations of motion, including falling bodies.
Use 9.8 m/s2 for free-fall acceleration in kinematics problems without air resistance.
Tell contact forces from non-contact forces.
Tell mass from weight.
Explain inertia as a body's resistance to changes in its motion and use it in daily examples.
Draw free-body diagrams and discuss the net force on an object.
State Newton's first law as the law of inertia.
Describe how a force can change an object's speed or direction.
State Newton's second law with acceleration and apply it to daily life.
State Newton's third law and explain action-reaction pairs.
State and use Newton's law of gravitation in problems.
Define and calculate gravitational field strength.
Calculate the mass of the Earth using the law of gravitation.
Explain why g decreases with height above the Earth.
Explain momentum and calculate it.
Relate net force to change in momentum and show how collision time affects the force.
State the law of conservation of momentum with everyday examples.
Define and calculate impulse.
Explain friction and what causes it.
Discuss the good and bad sides of friction in real life.
Analyse how friction dissipates energy, for example heating from rubbing.
Tell static from kinetic friction coefficients.
Compare rolling and sliding friction qualitatively.
Describe ways to reduce friction.

topics.title: Grade 9 Unit 4: Turning Effects of Forces

subtopics.title: Moment of a force and couples

outcomes.text: Tell like from unlike parallel forces.
Illustrate moment of force, moment arm and line of action with simple examples.
Solve problems on turning effects using force times perpendicular distance.
Define a couple, derive its formula and calculate it.
State and explain the principle of moments.
Explain equilibrium and its types.
Describe stable, unstable and neutral equilibrium with examples.
Analyse bodies in equilibrium using the principle of moments, such as weights on a metre rule.
Describe centre of mass and centre of gravity.
Analyse how the centre of gravity position affects the stability of simple objects.
Suggest how to make an object more stable by lowering its centre of mass and widening its base.
Define work done and illustrate it with examples.
Use W = Fd cos(theta) to solve problems and recognise types of work by angle.
Recall energy and its forms.
Define mechanical energy and list its types.
Define kinetic energy, derive its formula and use it.
Define gravitational potential energy and use its formula.
Explain elastic potential energy.
State the law of conservation of energy and discuss applications.
Use kinetic and gravitational potential energy formulae in simple energy conversions.
List renewable and non-renewable energy resources, especially in Pakistan.
Explain mechanical power and calculate it.
Explain efficiency.
Use the efficiency formula in simple energy-transfer problems.
Explain why no system can be 100% efficient.
Explain density and use it in simple problems.
Describe how to measure the density of liquids, regular solids and irregular solids using displacement.
Define and calculate pressure.
Describe how pressure varies with force and area in everyday cases.
Justify that the atmosphere exerts pressure.
Describe how atmospheric pressure changes with altitude.
Explain that changing atmospheric pressure can signal a weather change.
Derive p = rho g h for liquid pressure and solve problems.
State and explain Pascal's law.
Apply Pascal's law to hydraulic presses, lifts and brakes.
State Archimedes' principle and prove it.
State the principle of floatation and its conditions.
Apply Archimedes' principle to ships, submarines and hydrometers.
Explain stress and strain for elastic materials.
Explain Hooke's law.
Draw and read a stress-strain curve up to the elastic limit.

topics.title: Grade 9 Unit 7: Thermal Properties of Matter

outcomes.text: Describe plasma as the fourth state of matter.
Relate particle motion to temperature, including absolute zero as the lowest temperature.
Explain how a property that changes with temperature can be used to measure it.
Explain sensitivity, range and linearity of thermometers.
Tell good from poor conductors and give examples.
Explain convection in liquids and gases through density changes.
Explain how convection in seawater supports marine life.
Describe land and sea breezes and their moderating effect on coastal climates.
Explain how birds and gliders stay up by riding thermal currents.
Use convection to explain how cyclones form.
Explain magma flow in the Earth's mantle as convection.
Describe heat transfer by radiation, which needs no medium.
Describe how surface colour and texture affect emission, absorption and reflection of infrared.
Discuss how radiation emission depends on surface temperature and area.
Tell good from bad emitters and absorbers of radiation.
Analyse the greenhouse effect and its role in global warming.
Explain how global warming contributes to extreme weather.
Analyse everyday uses of conduction, convection and radiation such as pans, room heating, infrared thermometers and insulation.
Describe forces between magnetic poles and between magnets and magnetic materials.
Describe a magnetic field as a region where a magnetic pole feels a force.
Give examples of magnetic and non-magnetic materials.
Tell paramagnetic from diamagnetic materials by behaviour in a magnetic field.
Describe ferromagnetic materials and explain magnetisation using magnetic domains.
Explain qualitatively how materials are magnetised and demagnetised.
Tell temporary from permanent magnets.
Describe uses of permanent magnets and electromagnets.
Analyse the use of magnets in recording technology.
Define specific heat capacity, explain it and use Q = mc(delta T).
Analyse everyday effects of the large specific heat of water.
Describe changes of state between solid, liquid and gas, including sublimation and deposition.
Recall the melting and boiling temperatures of water at standard pressure.
Explain melting, freezing, boiling and condensation as energy transfer at constant temperature.
Explain thermal expansion with kinetic theory and compare expansion of solids, liquids and gases.
Describe linear and volumetric expansion of solids, qualitatively and quantitatively.
Explain thermal expansion of liquids as real and apparent expansion.
Analyse everyday applications and consequences of thermal expansion.
Describe evaporation as escape of energetic particles from a liquid surface.
Tell boiling from evaporation.
Analyse how temperature, humidity, surface area and air movement affect the evaporation rate.
Explain how evaporation causes cooling.
Describe cooling by evaporation in refrigeration without harmful CFCs.
Explain latent heat of fusion and vaporisation in terms of particles and calculate it.
Tell periodic, oscillatory and simple harmonic motion apart with examples.
Define displacement, amplitude, period and frequency for oscillations.
Show that frequency is the reciprocal of the time period.
Explain that SHM has acceleration proportional to displacement and opposite to it.
State the conditions needed for an object to oscillate with SHM.
Explain SHM using the ball-and-bowl example.
Show using forces on the bob that a small-amplitude pendulum moves with SHM.
Explain how a pendulum's period depends on length and g and not on mass.
Solve problems using T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g).
Describe wave motion using ropes, springs and water waves.
Show that waves carry energy without carrying matter.
Illustrate that in a transverse wave the vibration is at right angles to the energy flow.
Illustrate that in a longitudinal wave the vibration is parallel to the energy flow.
Describe wave features such as wavefront, wavelength, crest, trough, compression, rarefaction, amplitude and speed.
Apply the wave equation v = f x wavelength.
Describe reflection at a plane surface, refraction at a boundary and diffraction at a single slit.
Define pitch, loudness and quality of sound.
Define sound intensity and its SI unit.
Explain sound intensity level, use B = 10 log(I/I0) and the decibel.
Discuss why sound cannot travel in a vacuum.
Illustrate methods of measuring the speed of sound in air by distance and time.
State the audible range of humans as 20 Hz to 20000 Hz.
Describe that sound is generally faster in solids than liquids and in liquids than gases.
Define ultrasound and recall its uses, including medical diagnosis.
Explain the piezoelectric effect and its use in generating and detecting ultrasound.
Define infrasound and recall its uses, such as elephant communication and seismic study.
Explain why acoustic protection matters and how soft materials reduce echo.
Define refraction of light, normal, angle of incidence and angle of refraction.
Apply the rule that light bends toward the normal when slowing and away when speeding up.
Define and use refractive index as c/v.
Define refractive index through sin(i)/sin(r).
Explain critical angle and total internal reflection and the conditions for it.
Derive and use n = 1/sin(c).
Discuss optical fibres in telecommunications and their advantages.
Analyse how thin converging and diverging lenses act on a parallel beam.
Define focal length, principal axis and principal focus for lenses.
Tell real from virtual images.
Draw ray diagrams for a converging lens with the object at different positions.
Draw ray diagrams for a diverging lens.
Define and calculate linear magnification of a lens.
Use the lens formula for object distance, image distance and focal length.
Describe the use of a single lens as a magnifying glass.
Define power of a lens and its unit and calculate it.
Define resolving power and magnifying power.
Explain dispersion of light by a prism.
State the seven spectrum colours in order of frequency and wavelength.
Draw ray diagrams for the normal, short-sighted and long-sighted eye and give causes.
Describe how converging and diverging lenses correct long and short sight.
State that charges are positive and negative and that charge is quantised and measured in coulombs.
State that unlike charges attract and like charges repel.
Explain that charging solids by friction transfers negative charge.
State and apply Coulomb's law, including that it follows Newton's third law.
Explain how a conductor is charged by induction and earthing.
Suggest how charging and discharging is used in photocopiers, electrostatic precipitators and powder painting.
Define and calculate electric current as I = Q/t.
Explain conduction in metals by the movement of free electrons.
State that current is measured in amperes, coulombs per second.
Tell direct current from alternating current.
Tell conventional from electron current.
Explain and distinguish EMF from potential difference.
Calculate total EMF of sources in series and in parallel.
State and apply Ohm's law at constant temperature.
Define resistance and its unit and measure it with a voltmeter and ammeter.
Discuss factors affecting resistance and define resistivity.
Describe how temperature rise affects resistance, such as in a filament lamp.
Identify conductors, insulators and semiconductors by their ability to conduct.
Compare series and parallel resistor combinations for current, voltage and total resistance.
Calculate current, voltage and resistance in parts or all of a circuit.
Define electric power and use P = IV, I2R and V2/R.
Explain energy dissipation in resistors and use E = IVt.
Define the kilowatt-hour and relate it to the joule.
Calculate the cost of using appliances in kWh.
Explain why components need suitable power ratings.
State common electric hazards such as damaged insulation, overheating cables, damp and overloaded sockets.
Explain the harm electric shock does to the body.
State common uses of electricity such as heating, lighting, charging and powering motors.
Analyse the advantages of connecting lamps in parallel.
Explain trip switches and fuses and choose suitable fuse ratings.
Explain what happens when a live wire touches an earthed metal case.
Explain why appliance casings are either double-insulated or earthed.
State that a mains circuit has live, neutral and earth wires.
Explain why fuses and breakers go in the live wire.
Explain why domestic supplies are wired in parallel.
Describe the pattern and direction of the magnetic field of straight wires and solenoids.
Describe an experiment showing a force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
State and use Fleming's left-hand rule.
Describe fields and forces between parallel current-carrying conductors.
State that a coil in a magnetic field feels a turning effect and list factors that raise it.
Describe the construction and working of an electric motor with split-ring commutator and brushes.
State that the Earth's magnetic field is thought to come from its rotating molten iron core.
Describe electromagnetic induction and factors affecting the induced EMF.
Describe how AC generators work with slip rings and brushes.
Sketch and interpret EMF-time graphs for a simple AC generator.
Use period, frequency and peak value for alternating current or voltage.
Explain the construction and working of a simple iron-cored transformer.
Use Vp/Vs = Np/Ns.
Compare step-up and step-down transformers.
Explain high-voltage transmission to cut power loss and step-down transformers for safe supply.

units.title: Domain F: Space and Modern Physics

topics.title: Grade 10 Unit 8: Atomic and Nuclear Physics

outcomes.text: Describe the atom as a small positive nucleus of protons and neutrons with electrons in shells.
Analyse alpha-scattering results as evidence for a tiny, massive, positive nucleus in mostly empty space.
Define proton number Z and nucleon number A and find the number of neutrons.
Recall the term nuclide and use nuclide notation.
Explain isotopes and that an element can have several.
Explain what background radiation is.
State its main sources: radon, rocks and buildings, food and drink, cosmic rays.
Describe radioactivity as spontaneous emission of radiation by unstable nuclei.
Describe alpha, beta and gamma radiation and their behaviour in electric and magnetic fields.
Describe radioactive emission as spontaneous and random.
Compare alpha, beta and gamma radiation by ionising effect and penetrating power.
Explain radioactive decay as an unstable nucleus changing and emitting radiation.
Write and use nuclear decay equations in nuclide notation for alpha, beta and gamma emission.
Describe fission as splitting of a heavy nucleus and how released neutrons give a chain reaction.
Describe fusion as light nuclei combining, the main energy source of stars.
Recognise that mass converts to energy and use E = mc2 for energy released in nuclear reactions.
Explain half-life and find remaining nuclei from data, tables and decay curves.
Explain and apply carbon dating to estimate the age of ancient objects.

subtopics.title: Safe use and hazards of nuclear radiation

outcomes.text: Explain how radiation type and half-life decide isotope uses such as smoke alarms, food irradiation and thickness gauges.
State the effects of ionising radiation on living things, including cell death, mutations and cancer.
Explain safe movement, use and storage of radioactive materials using time, distance and shielding.
Explain the Sun as a medium-sized star of mostly hydrogen and helium radiating mainly infrared, visible and UV.
State that most matter in the universe is hypothesised to be dark matter.

units.title: Domain A: Physical Quantities and Measurement

outcomes.text: Describe the role of physics in space technology, nanotechnology, aerodynamics, medical physics, thermodynamics and solid-state physics.
Tell accuracy from precision by comparing sets of experimental data.
Explain why every measurement has some uncertainty because of instrument limits.
Estimate absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainties in combined results and keep suitable significant figures.
Check whether an equation is homogeneous using dimensions.
Define a unit vector and write vectors using i, j, k.
Describe multiplying a vector by a number.
Describe the scalar (dot) product of two vectors and its properties.
Describe the vector (cross) product, its properties and how to find its direction.
Analyse elastic collisions using conserved kinetic energy and equal relative speeds of approach and separation.
Show that momentum of an isolated system is conserved even if some kinetic energy changes.
Explain projectile motion without air resistance, with constant horizontal velocity and independent motions.
Find height, range, time of flight and best launch angle for projectiles.
Describe qualitatively how air resistance affects the range of a projectile.
Describe work as the scalar product of force and displacement.
Tell positive, negative and zero work apart and find work from a force-displacement graph.
Tell conservative from non-conservative forces.
Prove that the gravitational field is conservative.
Deduce the link between work and energy, with and without friction.
Show how gravitational potential leads to the potential energy of two point masses.
Define escape velocity, derive it and compute it for the Earth and Moon.
Derive power as force times velocity and solve problems.

topics.title: Grade 11 Unit 5: Rotational and Circular Motion

outcomes.text: Define the radian and convert between radians, degrees and revolutions.
Define and calculate angular displacement, velocity and acceleration, and link them to linear quantities.
Use equations of angular motion to solve problems.
Describe centripetal acceleration and its direction.
Define centripetal force, deduce its formulae and solve simple problems.
Analyse circular motion where tension, friction, gravity or a normal force supplies the centripetal force.
Explain how a centrifuge separates materials using centripetal force.

subtopics.title: Moment of inertia and angular momentum

outcomes.text: Define moment of inertia and angular momentum and calculate them for simple systems.
Derive and use the relation between torque, moment of inertia and angular acceleration.
Explain and apply conservation of angular momentum.
Analyse applications of angular momentum conservation such as flywheels, gyroscopes, skaters and divers.
Define rotational kinetic energy, derive its expression and use it.
Calculate average orbital speed from orbit radius and period.
Derive the relation between orbital period and radius using the law of gravitation.
Analyse geostationary orbits, including finding the orbital radius.
Define satellites and classify their types.
Explain why objects in orbiting satellites seem weightless.
Describe how artificial gravity counters weightlessness.
Explain why real fluids are viscous, linking viscosity to density and temperature.
Describe how viscous forces give a retarding force on a moving object.
Analyse how an object reaches terminal velocity.
State Stokes' law and derive terminal velocity of a sphere in a viscous fluid.
Explain why squeezing a pipe end speeds up the flow.
State and derive Bernoulli's equation.
Explain how changes in fluid speed cause pressure differences.
Analyse applications such as the Magnus effect, Venturi ducts and Torricelli's theorem.

topics.title: Grade 11 Unit 7: Mechanical Properties of Solids

outcomes.text: Tell crystalline, amorphous and polycrystalline solids apart by structure.
Describe deformation of solids in one dimension, tensile or compressive.
Explain Young's, bulk and shear modulus and use them in problems.
Use the area under a force-extension graph as work done.
Find elastic potential energy from the force-extension graph within the proportional limit.
Describe the basic assumptions of the kinetic theory of gases.
Apply the ideal gas equation of state, PV = nRT and PV = NkT.
Explain gas pressure from molecular motion and when an ideal gas approximates a real gas.
Calculate the root-mean-square speed of an ideal gas.
Derive and use the relation PV = (1/3)Nm<c2>.
Derive and use the average translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule.
Derive Boyle's and Charles's laws from kinetic theory.
State that regions in thermal equilibrium are at the same temperature.
Define internal energy of ideal and real gases and link temperature rise to it.
Tell work done by a system from work done on it.
Use W = P(delta V) for work done at constant pressure.
Explain qualitatively with particles how pressure, temperature and volume of a gas relate.
Define and use the first law of thermodynamics as conservation of energy.
Explain why Cp exceeds Cv and derive Mayer's relation.

subtopics.title: Heat engines and the second law

outcomes.text: Describe the working principle of a heat engine.
State and explain the second law, including the Kelvin and Clausius statements.
Describe the Carnot engine and its cycle on a PV diagram and its efficiency.
State that the Carnot cycle limits heat engine efficiency, eff = 1 - Tcold/Thot.
Describe a refrigerator as a reversed heat engine and its coefficient of performance.
Explain entropy as a measure of disorder and energy degradation.
Describe negentropy.
Describe that the projection of circular motion on a diameter is SHM.
Derive and use formulae for displacement, velocity and acceleration in SHM from circular motion.
Analyse graphs of displacement, velocity and acceleration in SHM.
Show with Hooke's law that a mass on a spring moves with SHM.
Derive and use angular frequency, period and frequency for a mass-spring system.
Describe how a resistive force damps oscillations.
Use light, critical and heavy damping and sketch their displacement-time graphs.
Describe practical examples of damping, such as critical damping in car suspension.
Explain resonance as maximum amplitude when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency.
Judge when resonance is useful, such as radio tuning, and when it must be avoided, such as bridges.
Analyse qualitatively how damping affects the sharpness of resonance.
Explain wave intensity as power per area and proportional to amplitude squared, and use it.
Derive and use the apparent frequency for a moving source or moving observer.
Apply the Doppler effect to radar, medical ultrasound and astronomy.
State and explain the principle of superposition for coherent waves.
Use superposition to explain noise-cancelling headphones.
Explain two-source interference with ripple tank, sound and light.
Analyse Young's double-slit fringes, including maxima, minima and fringe width.
Explain experiments showing stationary waves, nodes and antinodes.
Explain harmonics on a stretched string and quantised frequencies.
Explain harmonics in open and closed organ pipes.
Explain beats, calculate beat frequency and use it to tune instruments.
Describe diffraction of monochromatic light by a grating and its use to find wavelength.
Explain why white light gives spectral colours through a grating.
Use d sin(theta) = n lambda to solve grating problems.
Explain that polarisation applies to transverse waves.
Define and apply Malus's law for polarising filters.
Explain the use of polaroids in sky photography and stress analysis.

units.title: Domain F: Space and Modern Physics

topics.title: Grade 11 Unit 11: Relativity and Particle Physics

outcomes.text: Tell inertial from non-inertial frames of reference with examples.
Explain that a constant light speed makes measurements of space and time relative to the observer.
State the postulates of special relativity.
Explain the consequences of special relativity: simultaneity, mass-energy, length contraction, time dilation, mass increase.
Solve simple problems using the consequences of special relativity.
State that space-time treats time as a fourth dimension and that its distortions have observable effects.
State that nucleon number and charge are conserved in nuclear processes.
Describe the composition, mass and charge of alpha, beta and gamma radiations.
Explain that an antiparticle has the same mass and opposite charge, such as the positron.
Describe quarks and antiquarks and the six quark flavours.
Describe protons and neutrons by their quark composition.
Define hadrons, leptons and bosons with examples.
Explain the working principle and uses of particle accelerators.
State that an electric field is a field of force.
Define and calculate electric field strength using E = F/q and E = kQ/r2.
Represent electric fields with field lines.
Describe field direction around a point charge, a charged sphere and between parallel plates.
Find and justify the null point where the net field is zero.
Describe the effect of a uniform electric field on charged particles.
Explain how a Faraday cage shields its inside from external fields.
Explain electrical breakdown as ionisation of a gas in a strong field.
State that corona discharge and Lichtenberg figures are examples of breakdown.
Explain how lightning is generated.
Explain how a lightning rod protects people.
Define electric potential and potential difference.
Show that field equals the negative potential gradient.
Derive the potential due to a point charge.
Explain how potential leads to the electric potential energy of two point charges.
Solve simple problems on electric potential and potential energy.
Define and calculate capacitance of spheres and parallel plates.
Derive and apply capacitance for series and parallel combinations.
Find energy stored in a capacitor from the area under the potential-charge graph.
Analyse charging and discharging graphs of a capacitor through a resistor with time constant RC.
List uses of capacitors in household appliances.
Use I = nqAv to find the current in a conductor.
Explain emf, internal resistance and terminal potential difference of a cell.
Use V = E - Ir and explain when terminal voltage is below, equal to or above EMF.
Discuss the temperature coefficient of resistivity for metals and semiconductors.
Justify and use colour codes for resistors.
Explain how conducting carbon fibres let inspectors check concrete bridges.
Describe superconductivity and its practical uses.
Explain the use of thermistors and LDRs in potential dividers and sensors.
State Kirchhoff's first law as conservation of charge.
State Kirchhoff's second law as conservation of energy.
Use Kirchhoff's laws to solve single- and two-loop circuits.
Analyse potential dividers, including R1/R2 = V1/V2.
Explain null methods with a galvanometer and the Wheatstone bridge.
Describe how a potentiometer compares potentials without drawing current.

topics.title: Grade 12 Unit 3: Magnetic Fields and Electromagnetism

subtopics.title: Magnetic force on currents and charges

outcomes.text: Use F = BIL sin(theta) for a current-carrying conductor and define magnetic flux density.
Describe a charged particle in a uniform magnetic field and use F = qvB sin(theta).
Explain how electric and magnetic fields work in velocity selectors.
Define magnetic flux as flux density times perpendicular area.
State and derive Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction.
Use Lenz's law to predict induced current direction as conservation of energy.
Use Faraday's and Lenz's laws to solve problems.
Explain how a seismometer detects earthquakes by electromagnetic induction.
Apply that mean power in a resistor is half the peak power for sinusoidal AC.
Explain r.m.s. values as the DC equivalent for heating and use Irms = I0/sqrt2 and Vrms = V0/sqrt2.
Explain phase of AC and phase leads and lags.
Explain AC in resistors, capacitors and inductors using graphs and phasor diagrams and discuss power dissipation.
Identify inductors as chokes that oppose alternating current.
Calculate the reactance of capacitors and inductors.
Describe impedance as the phasor sum of resistance and reactance in series RC and RL circuits.
Tell intrinsic from extrinsic semiconductors, P-type and N-type, and how electrons and holes conduct.
Explain the structure and working of a PN junction diode under forward and reverse bias.
Tell half-wave from full-wave rectification graphically.
Explain half-wave rectification with a single diode.
Explain full-wave rectification with a four-diode bridge.
Identify the structure and symbols of NPN and PNP transistors.
Describe the functions of emitter, base and collector in a properly biased transistor.
Recognise common-emitter, common-base and common-collector configurations.
Describe the NPN transistor as a switch and why transistors suit digital devices.
Compare analogue and digital electronics.
Explain that electronic devices are built from digital logic circuits acting as switches.
Explain Boolean logic as the basis for converting analogue to digital data, including bits and bytes.
State the action of AND, OR, NAND, NOR and NOT gates in words and truth tables.
Identify uses of logic gates for security such as burglar alarms.
Identify and draw standard symbols for basic logic gates.
Combine Boolean switches to achieve logical operations in given problems.

units.title: Domain F: Space and Modern Physics

outcomes.text: State the speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum and air.
Use E = hf to find photon energy in joules or electron volts.
Explain photon momentum p = E/c and use it.
Describe photoelectron emission from a metal lit by electromagnetic radiation.
Describe why classical wave theory cannot explain the photoelectric effect.
Describe and use threshold frequency and threshold wavelength.
Explain that emission needs photon energy at least equal to the work function.
Explain emission with photon energy and work function and find maximum kinetic energy.
Explain why maximum kinetic energy is independent of intensity while current depends on it.
Draw and interpret graphs of kinetic energy vs frequency and current vs intensity.
Describe the Compton effect, where scattered X-rays and gamma rays gain wavelength.
Solve problems using the Compton wavelength shift equation.
Explain pair production and find the minimum photon energy needed.
Describe pair annihilation producing gamma rays with energy and momentum conserved.
Calculate the gamma photon energy from electron-positron annihilation.
Analyse the evidence for wave-particle duality of light.
Explain how electron diffraction shows the wave nature of particles.
Explain and apply the de Broglie wavelength.
Understand that isolated atoms such as hydrogen have discrete electron energy levels.
Tell continuous, line and band spectra apart.
Tell absorption from emission spectra.
Explain the formation of emission and absorption line spectra for hydrogen.
Use hf = energy difference to find energy levels, frequency and wavelength.
Explain how electron microscopes achieve very high resolution.
Explain Heisenberg's uncertainty principle qualitatively.
Use the uncertainty principle to explain why measurements are necessarily uncertain.
Explain X-ray production by electron bombardment and find the minimum wavelength from voltage.
Explain the use of X-rays in imaging the body, including contrast.
Explain how CT scanning builds a 3D image.
Define and use mass defect and binding energy.
Sketch binding energy per nucleon against nucleon number.
Recall what nuclear fusion and fission are.
Explain how binding energy per nucleon relates to fission and fusion.
Compare the energy released in fission with that of a chemical reaction.
Explain the fission chain reaction and its control in a reactor with coolant, moderator and control rods.
Describe the main parts of a water-moderated power reactor.
Explain why uranium fuel must be enriched.
Calculate energy released in nuclear reactions using delta m c2.
Explain that fluctuating count rates show the randomness of decay.
Define activity and decay constant.
State and use A = lambda N.
Use lambda = 0.693/half-life to solve problems.
Describe the exponential nature of decay and use x = x0 e^(-lambda t).
Explain what a medical tracer is.
Illustrate how PET scanning works via positron-electron annihilation.
Explain that annihilation gamma photons leave the body and are detected to image tracer concentration.
Apply the inverse square law for radiant flux.
Define and use standard candles to find distances to galaxies.

subtopics.title: Black body radiation and stellar properties

outcomes.text: Explain blackbody radiation.
State and apply Wien's displacement law to estimate a star's surface temperature.
State and apply the Stefan-Boltzmann law.
Estimate the radius of a star from Wien's and Stefan-Boltzmann laws.
Explain why spectral lines of distant objects appear at longer wavelengths than in the lab.
Explain how redshift suggests the Universe is expanding and solve related problems.
State and explain Hubble's law and how it leads to the Big Bang theory.
